_note: Hand-written GENERATED questions (not from NESA papers) for areas templates don't cover well: multi-step and challenging problems. Answers are machine-checkable.

questions.text: An arithmetic sequence and a geometric sequence both have first term 2. The 3rd term of the arithmetic sequence equals the 2nd term of the geometric sequence, and the 4th term of the arithmetic sequence equals the 3rd term of the geometric sequence. Given that the common ratio \(r \ne 1\), find \(r\).
questions.concept: Once you link the AP and GP conditions, you get simultaneous equations in \(d\) and \(r\).
questions.technique: Write down each sequence's general term before you equate anything, then use the given restriction to throw out a root.

common_errors.diagnosis: The question rules out \(r = 1\), so that root has to go.

questions.text: For the curve \(y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 5\), find the coordinates of the point of inflection. Enter as a list \(x, y\).
steps: \(y'' = 0\) at \(x = 1\); \(y''\) changes sign from negative to positive, so concavity changes.
questions.concept: Curve sketching is systematic: \(y'\) gives you turning points, and \(y''\) gives you concavity and inflections.
questions.technique: Justify the inflection by showing the sign change of \(y''\) in a table.

questions.text: The function \(f(x) = |x - 2|\) is continuous at \(x = 2\). Is it differentiable at \(x = 2\)? Answer 'yes' or 'no' as option A (yes) or B (no).
steps: The left-hand gradient is \(-1\) and the right-hand gradient is \(+1\).
The gradients from each side differ (a sharp corner), so \(f\) is not differentiable at \(x = 2\).
questions.concept: For differentiability the left and right gradients have to agree. Being continuous isn't enough.
questions.technique: Compare the one-sided limits of the gradient.

questions.text: An open box is made from a \(12\) cm by \(12\) cm square of card by cutting equal squares of side \(x\) cm from each corner and folding up the sides. Find the value of \(x\) that maximises the volume.
steps: \(V'\) changes from positive to negative at \(x = 2\), so a maximum: \(x = 2\) cm (volume 128 cm³).
questions.concept: Optimisation runs in four moves: build the model, restrict the domain, differentiate, then justify that you have a maximum.
questions.technique: State the domain of \(x\) early. It's your reason for rejecting \(x = 6\).

common_errors.diagnosis: At \(x = 6\) the base disappears and the volume is zero, so use the domain to reject it.

questions.text: Find the area enclosed between \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 2x + 3\).
steps: The line is above the parabola between them.
questions.concept: The area between two curves is \(\int (\text{upper} - \text{lower})\,dx\), taken between their intersection points.
questions.technique: Find the intersections first, then work out which curve is on top.

common_errors.diagnosis: You've subtracted the wrong way round. It should be upper minus lower.

questions.text: A particle moves with displacement \(x = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t\) metres. Find the total distance travelled in the first 4 seconds.
steps: \(v = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 3(t-1)(t-3)\): the particle changes direction at \(t = 1\) and \(t = 3\).
questions.concept: Distance travelled adds up the length of each leg between changes of direction. Displacement doesn't do that.
questions.technique: Find when \(v = 0\) first, then work out \(x\) at each of those times.

common_errors.diagnosis: That's the displacement \(x(4) - x(0)\), not the distance travelled.
